cases.rationale: Executes one initial SQL, returns immediately on success, and on failure sends the exact execution feedback with schema and question to a repair request.
Uses a single initial draft and conditionally repairs only after a failed execute result, preserving the failed SQL and feedback in the second prompt.
Runs the initial SQL but discards the execution result and never performs a repair after failure.
Makes an unconditional extra n=2 request regardless of whether execution succeeded, which violates the success path and adds batch sampling.
Requests three candidates, executes all three, and selects by majority over execution-result signatures rather than by prompt order.
Builds three candidates through separate prompts, executes every candidate, and returns the candidate matching the majority execution outcome.
Requests three candidates but returns the first without executing candidates or arbitrating by execution evidence.
Chooses among candidate SQL strings lexically and never uses execution results, so it is string voting rather than result voting.
First asks for relevant schema elements, derives a reduced schema from that payload, and passes the linked evidence and reduced schema to final SQL generation.
Obtains two linked-subset payloads, uses them to reduce the schema, and supplies both payloads plus the reduced schema in the final prompt.
Calls a linking step but ignores its payload and sends the full schema into final SQL generation.
Skips linked-schema selection entirely and explicitly considers every table in the complete schema.
Uses one sample and explicitly preserves the original question and schema while treating any Hint as an added requirement outside the original wording.
Uses a single LLM call with a system instruction that keeps the question and schema intact and applies Hint text as a hard extra constraint.
Only passes schema and question through without making the Hint visible as a distinct explicit requirement.
Actively instructs the model to ignore any Hint text, contradicting the guarded-hint mechanism.
Requests two differently framed SQL constructions, executes both, prefers the first when it has rows, and otherwise selects using observed execution results.
Requests two semantically different constructions, executes both, returns the first when both are usable, and falls back based on execution evidence.
Creates the second view by adding whitespace to the first SQL, which is not an independent construction.
Executes two requested SQL candidates but returns the second regardless of execution results, ignoring the required arbitration.
Parses a JSON-list plan, answers each step in order with prior partials, and passes the collected partial answers into final SQL assembly.
Builds an ordered two-step plan, collects intermediate facts sequentially, and requires final SQL generation to incorporate those facts.
Gets a plan but final generation uses only step titles, so no partial-answer payload can influence the final SQL.
Calls subtask prompts but discards their outputs and omits all partial answers from final SQL generation.
On success it avoids repair; on failure it assigns one explicit category and uses a category-specific repair action with exact feedback.
Classifies failed execution feedback into exactly one category and then applies a distinct syntax, schema, or semantics repair prompt.
On failure it lists all possible categories and asks for a generic correction rather than making one explicit classification and targeted action.
Computes a category but uses the same generic edit action for every category, so category-specific action templates are absent.
Preserves schema and question while explicitly requiring one SQL code fence and no extra explanatory text.
Uses a single-call system instruction that requires exactly one fenced SQL block and nothing outside it, while passing schema and question.
Only passes schema and question through and never imposes an explicit fenced-SQL/no-extra-text output constraint.
Explicitly forbids a SQL code fence and asks for explanation, contradicting the format guard requirement.
